messages:
Molly (oncall): heads up — getting a customer escalation: hosted API returning lots of 504s and p95s spiking to ~15s. dashboards show request_queue_depth hitting the configured limit and then tail timeouts. digging into gateway logs now.

ops-bot: ALERT: hosted-gateway request_q depth high (instance=gw-08) — depth=4096, reject_rate=0.12, avg_enqueue_latency=250ms

Samir (infra): which model/route? is this across tenants or one customer?

Molly (oncall): looks concentrated on /v1/generate for model oak-13b-quant in us-west; tenant id t-42 shows the majority. but there are some cross-tenant spikes correlated with same route.

Jordan (runtime): probable continuous-batching backlog — KV cache spin + long contexts cause batchers to hold tokens and queue up. logs: 
```
[gw-08] enqueue req_id=5f3a depth=4096 model=oak-13b-quant seq_len=1024 kv_cache_load=1 batch_wait_ms=1200
[batcher-3] pending_batches=85 oldest_wait_ms=4800
```

Samir (infra): quick mitigation: temporarily reduce max_batch_ms and disable continuous batching for that model, or increase queue_depth threshold + autoscaler headroom. can we flip that via admin API?

Jordan (runtime): yes — we can toggle continuous batching per model. example (do in staging then prod):
```
curl -X POST "https://internal-admin.redwood/api/models/oak-13b-quant/config" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"continuous_batching": false, "max_batch_ms": 8}'
```

Molly (oncall): Ana — customer already opened a support ticket, they reported ~40s timeouts and request errors in their app. can you coordinate a credit and let them know we're mitigating?

Ana (support): on it. I've flagged support-PRIORITY and sent the customer the temporary mitigation steps (fallback model suggestion + expect 15–20m for config change). opening ticket INC-34411. copying CSM.

Samir (infra): FYI autoscaler didn't kick because reserved_pool_utilization was at 98% and we hit tenant commit caps — need ops approval to burst extra capacity. I'm increasing pool_target from 120 -> 160 on gw-pool-3 for the next 30m.

ops-bot: CHANGE: pool-target updated (pool=gw-pool-3 old=120 new=160) by Samir.

Jordan (runtime): added a temporary routing rule to divert 10% of oak-13b traffic to oak-7b-fallback to reduce pressure while we stabilize:
```
PATCH /internal-routing
{
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "model": "oak-13b-quant",
  "fallback": "oak-7b-fallback",
  "percent": 10
}
```

Molly (oncall): requeue/backpressure observed drop_rate -> 0.02 after changes but p95 still elevated. need deep trace capture from gw-08 and batcher-3 for last 15m. Jordan can you grab traces and KV cache stats?

Jordan (runtime): pulling traces now — uploading to s3://incidents/1718209876/traces.tar.gz. KV cache shows repeated cold miss spikes when tenant t-42 toggles long contexts; the batcher backlog correlates with multi-turn streams. repro script added below:
```
# repro: 200 concurrent clients, seq_len=1024
python tools/spike.py --concurrency 200 --model oak-13b-quant --seq 1024 --duration 60
```

Samir (infra): long-term fix suggestions: enforce per-tenant concurrency caps for heavy-context routes, add adaptive queue weighting by token length, and surface kvcache hit-rate to routing decisions. filing infra task INF-726.

Ana (support): customer accepted temporary fallback and appreciated the proactive credit offer. asked for ETA on permanent fix — we'll update once postmortem and roadmap item are scheduled.

Molly (oncall): next steps: Jordan to collect traces + open runtime postmortem (PM-incident), Samir to follow up on autoscaler headroom and pool policy, Ana to close customer loop. Ops, if queue depth spikes again, escalate to oncall with runbook step-1 (disable continuous batching for model).

Samir (infra): noted. also capturing metrics to identify if other tenants show similar pattern — will run a 24h cohort analysis.

ops-bot: ACTION: runtime config change applied (continuous_batching=false) for model oak-13b-quant by Jordan at 1718209950 — deploy id=cfg-9a7c — no rollback required.

Molly (oncall): closing the immediate escalation — monitoring for 2 hours, will file follow-ups. thanks team.
